findings.finding: ESICM recommendation against routine continuous NMBA omitted non-COVID adult scope.
findings.resolution: Final bilingual text limits this to moderate/severe non-COVID adult ARDS; COVID evidence does not support a recommendation either way. ATS early severe conditional guidance retained.

findings.finding: Seven treatment benefit/risk/action claims were mislabelled explanation.
findings.resolution: treatment3/4/5 and medications1/2/4/5 correctly classified; actual independent authoring-source support checked.

findings.finding: Earlier ATS2017 ECMO/recruitment and nonspecific education could be overgeneralised to present treatment.
findings.resolution: Only still-retained low-volume/pressure and prone portions used; current ATS2024/ESICM2023 define present regional differences. No oxygen, ventilator, steroid or nutrition self-prescription introduced.

findings.finding: Hospital worsening action initially cited two NHLBI pages from one authoring group.
findings.resolution: Added independently written NHS ARDS immediate-action/hospital-treatment support; inpatient alerting the existing team implements the same worsening-breathing emergency action.

scope_decisions.rationale: Acute inflammatory hypoxaemic respiratory failure, adult and paediatric routes, trigger-specific care and ICU recovery are covered. Neonatal surfactant deficiency KB23.0 remains distinct, not inflated into this leaf.

independence: ATS/ESICM/SCCM/PALICC-2/ESPEN separately authored panels share studies and some authors; ATS2017 joint guideline counts once. NIH pages one group; Mayo/ATS education cites NIH and common sources. NHS pregnancy links UKTIS, explicit common basis retained. ASHP authors prednisone page; MedlinePlus only hosts. No two-source pair is claimed to be independent trial replication.
resolution: Accept exact candidate for evidence-based editorial integration, not clinician sign-off.

dispute_adjudication.resolution: Adult ATS2024/ESICM2023 NMBA differences include non-COVID versus COVID scope; steroid adult/pediatric recommendations remain distinct; no universal drug/dose/duration or guaranteed ECMO benefit.
